subject: physics
question_text: State Boyle's law and Charles's law.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Very Short Answer Question 4 (printed p.136). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: Boyle's law (PV = constant at fixed temperature) and Charles's law (V/T = constant at fixed pressure) are both stated with the correct held-constant quantity named, matching NCERT Class-11 Chapter 13.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Boyle's law
lines: of a fixed mass of gas is inversely
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the quantity held constant, then state the inverse proportionality.
steps.why: Held at constant temperature, molecules strike the walls with the same average speed. Squeezing the gas into a smaller volume packs the same molecules closer, so they strike the walls more often and the pressure rises exactly enough to keep PV fixed.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to state temperature is held constant — without it, PV = constant does not hold.
Writing pressure is proportional to volume instead of inversely proportional.

recall.must_convey: That at constant temperature the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its volume, PV equals constant.

steps.memory_tip: Boyle: same temperature, squeeze the volume, the pressure goes up to match.

steps.label: Charles's law
lines: At constant pressure, the volume of
a fixed mass of gas is directly
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name the quantity held constant, then state the direct proportionality with absolute temperature.
steps.why: Held at constant pressure, heating the gas raises the average speed of its molecules. To keep the pressure the same, the gas must occupy a larger volume, so volume rises in step with the absolute temperature.
common_mistakes: Using the Celsius temperature. T must be the absolute temperature in kelvin.
Forgetting to state pressure is held constant for this law.

recall.must_convey: That at constant pressure the volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature, V by T equals constant.

steps.memory_tip: Charles: same pressure, heat it up, the volume grows to match — T in kelvin.

insider_note: Name the quantity held constant in each law — that is where the marks are, not just the two formulas.
